concepts.name: Judging compost maturity by smell/color/feel
concepts.open_problem: The 'look, smell and feel' of finished compost (dark/earthy vs sour/ammonia) is the field-level readiness test used by gardeners and operators, but it is explicitly acknowledged as unreliable and gives little information about true degree of maturation versus lab/process indicators.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen as a shipping product; an Alibaba product-insights page discusses an 'AI-powered compost readiness detector app' concept and research e-noses exist, but e-noses are stated to lack precision and no consumer app reliably replaces tactile/odor judgment
concepts.verbatim_quote: The look, the smell and the feel of the finished product gives an indication of the maturity, though these techniques are not very reliable.

concepts.name: Knowing when a qanat needs cleaning/maintenance (tacit muqanni knowledge)
concepts.open_problem: Qanats need annual de-silting judged and performed by skilled muqanni who enter shafts and even invented tools to gauge water flow and irrigation timing; this body of traditional construction/maintenance knowledge is documented as being lost with no instrumented replacement.
concepts.verbatim_quote: Knowledge of building qanats and maintaining them is being lost.

concepts.name: Manual scrap-metal identification by spark test
concepts.open_problem: Ferrous/alloy classification by grinding a sample and reading spark color, volume, nature and length against known samples is a fast cheap human-skill end point, but it cannot positively identify a material (chemistry needed) and depends on the operator's trained eye.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen as a phone app for a human's spark read; instead AI bypasses the skill via optical-emission-spectrometry ML (arXiv 1903.09415, F1 ~96.9%) and camera sorters (EverSteel ~20+ categories) at the plant level
concepts.verbatim_quote: The important spark characteristics are color, volume, nature of the spark, and length.

concepts.name: Reading aquaculture pond water quality by color/smell
concepts.open_problem: Experienced farmers judge pond health from water color (green shades = productive, clear = unproductive) and smell (sulfur = oxygen-depletion emergency); it is explicitly a subjective human-eye indicator used where no sensing system exists.
concepts.app_market_check: app exists (XpertSea smartphone app; AquaEasy, AquaPulse, HydroNeo AI water-quality/disease platforms) but these lean on sensors/growth models; a 2022 vision-based water-color ID system is research-stage, not the human color/smell judgment
concepts.verbatim_quote: For an experienced farmer, water color is a subjective indicator that can represent water quality and can be directly observed by human eyes when no water quality sensing system is built.

concepts.name: Anaerobic digester health read by foaming/scum and operator vigilance
concepts.open_problem: Operators must spot precursors of a digester upset (foaming/scum, VFA rise, alkalinity drift) before catastrophic foaming; pH explicitly does NOT give early warning, so judgment leans on watching scum/foam and acid-alkalinity ratios over time.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen as a consumer/commercial app; vendor troubleshooting guides + lab test kits (Aquafix/Digester Doc) dominate rather than an AI app predicting the upset
concepts.verbatim_quote: Most catastrophic foaming episodes don't appear without warning, and vigilant operators can spot several precursors that indicate a major foaming event may be imminent.

concepts.name: Irrigation scheduling by feel-of-soil and crop look
concepts.open_problem: Traditional scheduling squeezes root-zone soil into a ball/ribbon by hand and reads crop appearance to decide when/how much to water; it lacks a scientific basis and tends to over-irrigate, yet experienced farmers can match sensor results - an unquantified embodied skill.
concepts.app_market_check: apps exist for sensor/ET-based scheduling, but tools that replicate the bare-hand feel-of-soil ribbon judgment are not seen; the manual feel method remains a human skill
concepts.verbatim_quote: The feel and appearance method involves taking a soil sample by hand to estimate moisture content based on how the soil ribbons or clumps.

concepts.name: Manual MRF picking / hand identification of mixed waste
concepts.open_problem: Trained human pickers at material recovery facilities visually identify and pull items machines cannot yet distinguish (textiles, hazardous items, specific plastics); this experiential identification is limited by fatigue/boredom and human-factor variability.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen as an app; automation is plant-scale robotic/optical sorters that 'gradually replaced' hand sorting rather than aiding the human picker's judgment
concepts.verbatim_quote: Automated sorting gradually replaced hand sorting based on manual labor and worker experience because of its precise identification and efficient separation.

concepts.name: Water dowsing / witching to site a well
concepts.open_problem: Locating groundwater by walking with a forked stick or L-rods that 'respond' over water is a persistent folk practice; it is a tacit bodily judgment with no scientific merit per USGS/NGWA, yet still used to site wells.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen (no credible app; practice is scientifically rejected, so the 'gap' is that the human ritual persists despite no validity)
concepts.verbatim_quote: The National Ground Water Association, in a position statement, "strongly opposes the use of water witches to locate groundwater on the grounds that controlled experimental evidence clearly indicates that the technique is totally without scientific merit".

concepts.name: Pinpointing buried water-main leaks by ear (listening stick)
concepts.open_problem: Leak technicians localize buried-pipe leaks by listening; different pipe materials and leak types make distinct sounds and bigger leaks 'feather out', so accurate pinpointing requires an experienced ear that not all leaks even satisfy (some are inaudible).
concepts.app_market_check: electronic amplified listening sticks/correlators are sold as hardware (Gutermann, HWM, FCS) that augment the ear, but the interpretive skill stays human; no consumer app replaces it
concepts.verbatim_quote: While all water leaks produce sounds, different types of leaks produce different sounds, and you must be experienced to hear leaks.

notes: Least AI-touched / fertile gaps: (1) qanat maintenance know-how (muqanni) = ai_penetration none, documented as actively being LOST, no instrument substitute; (2) water dowsing = none but scientifically void, so it's a persistence-of-ritual gap rather than a real capability to automate; (3) anaerobic-digester foaming foresight = low, leans on operator vigilance, pH explicitly NOT an early warning - strong tacit/temporal judgment with only lab kits, no predictive app seen. Moderately touched but human judgment still primary: spark-test (AI exists via OES/cameras at plant scale, NOT as a phone app for the human spark read), aquaculture color/smell (sensor apps exist but color/smell judgment itself research-stage), feel-of-soil irrigation (sensor/ET apps exist, hand-ribbon judgment not replicated), manual MRF picking (automated at plant scale, not aiding the human). Compost maturity by smell/feel = low and notable because sources themselves call the human test 'not very reliable' yet it remains the field default and e-noses 'lack the precision'. Honest caveat: app_market_check distinguishes plant/industrial AI (often present) from a consumer/phone product reproducing the specific sensory judgment (mostly absent). Most quotes are from Wikipedia or primary practice/research sources; aquaculture and leak quotes are from PMC/WaterWorld rather than Wikipedia.
